answered_questions.Q3: ANSWERED 2026-09-05 by measurement: a host unix socket bind-mounted into a container is INVISIBLE inside it on this host. Host holds srwxr-xr-x and a host nc -U returns the greeting; the container gets an empty dir and 'cannot statx'. Docker Desktop's VM does not project a socket inode across its shared filesystem, so classifyPeer is never reached and 4.3's fail-open worry is unreachable by this route. On Linux it would read a real uid and DENY a worker's 10001 against the operator's uid, which is fail-closed.
answered_questions.Q6: ANSWERED 2026-09-05 by the owner: SPLIT THE AXES. SUPERSEDES the 'no coverage datum' clause of the D8/Q9 entry above, which was answered 2026-09-04 and is now only correct about the VERDICT LATTICE: no new terminal state was added, but coverage IS now a datum beside the verdict. q4_probe_2026_09_04.arm_1_children_settle: ANSWERED YES. The actor was SIGKILLed with the fan-out complete; all three reviewers had already settled idle and written result envelopes. Children are independently dispatched tasks with their own supervisors, so the actor's death does not touch them.
q4_probe_2026_09_04.arm_2_replies_partial: NOT CLEANLY MEASURED, and saying so rather than claiming it. /replies did end 2-of-3 and the restart did not repair it - but the third reply was never going to land for an unrelated reason (see the defect below), and lang had settled 3m37s BEFORE the kill. So this run cannot separate 'the actor died before carrying a reply' from 'there was no reply to carry'. A clean measurement needs the kill to land between a child settling with a VALID envelope and its reply being copied.
q4_probe_2026_09_04.arm_3_replay_or_redispatch: ANSWERED: REPLAY, cleanly. After the restart every child's inbox envelope was still epoch=2 attempt=1 - no re-dispatch - and the relay logged 'already dispatched, unchanged' on every subsequent pass. The SRD's bar ('a design that cannot answer the third has no idempotency') is met.
q4_probe_2026_09_04.L6_detached: ANSWERED: REAL. The relay's launching shell had exited; ps showed PPID=1 and PGID=self, so it was reparented and is its own process-group leader. Engineer B fixed this in code and could not probe it.

defect_found.what: An unparseable result envelope silently deletes an entire lens, and the collation then blames the reviewer for it.
defect_found.evidence: rev-lang-1 wrote a real 3906-byte review ('five findings, worst being partial credential reda...') into result.json containing `[\w\\-_]+` - a regex quoted into a JSON string, so `\w` is an invalid JSON escape. The harvester could not parse it, the verdict became `unknown`, the relay's collation brief said 'lang settled unknown and produced no report', and the collation recorded reported:false with that note.
defect_found.why_it_matters: Every layer behaved correctly and the record is still wrong: the note attributes to the LENS a failure that was a serialisation error, and the operator reading `partial` learns the wrong thing. Nothing logged the parse failure - the relay log mentions it zero times.
defect_found.why_it_is_structural: The language reviewer is the seat most likely to hit it, because it is the one whose job is quoting code. A regex in a JSON string needs double-escaping and this one had no reason to know that.
defect_found.fix_direction: Two, and they are separable: (1) the harvester must distinguish 'no envelope' from 'an envelope that would not parse', and say which - the second is a worker-authored file that exists and can be named with its parse error; (2) the collation's lens note must not attribute a transport or serialisation failure to the reviewer.

FIXED.F4_relay_start_lock: REAL, MEDIUM. acquireRelayLock answered EEXIST with null and never opened the file, so the pid it writes was read by nobody: one hard crash left review-relay.lock behind forever and no relay could start until a human deleted it — the permanently-actorless console the module exists to prevent. Reachable: I SIGKILLed a relay during the Q4 probe. Also leaked the descriptor if writeFile threw. Fixed with the record's own (pid, start-time) identity; unreadable is NOT stale; takeover is remove-and-reclaim so the kernel picks the winner. Two mutations, both killed — stealing any lock reddens two tests.
FIXED.F7_harvest_swallow: REAL, LOW. The dispatch arm captures its rejection reason into the child's note; the harvest arm emitted one fixed sentence and dropped it, so a torn state.json was reported with less information than a refused dispatch. Now carries the reason. This is the route ISC-517 named as still open.
FIXED.F10_inbox_catch: REAL, LOW, and it cost me a day. One catch spanned ENOENT, bad JSON and a schema failure and reported all three as 'no dispatch record'. My own probe of the production harvest hit exactly this and was sent hunting a dispatch that never happened. Now distinguishes absent from unreadable.
FIXED.arch_journal_write: REAL. relay-journal wrote with a bare writeFile; the journal reader fails closed, so a torn write BLOCKS the collator until a person deletes the file. Now writeJsonAtomic. Rename is safe here and forbidden on the reply plane — the journal is host-side under relay/ and mounted into nothing; that distinction is now written beside the call.
FIXED.F14_servesConsole_visibility: The FINDING was wrong but the code changed anyway — see DISPROVED.

DISPROVED.F14_servesConsole_collision: FALSE POSITIVE, and instructive. The reviewer read `join("")` and filed a set-encoding collision: ['ab','c'] and ['a','bc'] both render 'abc'. The source actually contained join("\x01") — a literal 0x01 byte, invisible to sed, to a diff, to a terminal and to my own grep, which also found nothing. The implementation was correct all along. I replaced the raw byte with the escape \u0001: byte-identical at runtime, and now visible, so the next reader cannot re-file it. The test is kept because it pins a real property and reddens if the separator is removed.

VERIFIED_NOT_FIXED.F5_publishReply_unguarded: REAL, MEDIUM. The collation dispatch is wrapped in try/catch -> collation_failed with a docblock arguing at length why a throw there is wrong; the publishReply loop twenty lines earlier, the other last-hop effect in the same pass, is bare. For the ENOENT case the adapter names (console not built) retry is right; for EACCES/ENOSPC/a wedged mount it is the unbounded non-converging retry collation_failed exists to prevent. NOT FIXED because the adapter wraps ENOENT into a plain Error, so classifying needs a typed error across adapter+relay — a design change, not a patch.
VERIFIED_NOT_FIXED.F6_exhaustiveness: REAL, MEDIUM. Four if-chains with unconditional tails will misclassify a new union variant silently.
